transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for taking the time to see me. It's really nice to meet you, too. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been having this feeling lately that I can’t really seem to settle in my own body anymore? It sounds a little silly to say out loud, and it's probably just normal stress, but I really notice it when I’m supposed to just sit quietly and handle things like paperwork or, you know, sitting down to go over shared household plans. I just get this sort of restless feeling and I can't seem to just be still. 

I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the kind of thing people usually come in for?
Have you felt this kind of restlessness since childhood?

Oh, um... childhood. Well, yes, I suppose so. Looking back, I think it’s actually always been a part of me, even way back in elementary school. I mean, I don't want to sound like I was a difficult child or anything—I really always tried my best to be good! But... well, I was definitely the girl who always had a terribly messy desk. And, um,
Did you often have trouble paying attention in class when you were a child?

Oh, um... paying attention? I'm not entirely sure about that one, to be honest. I always really wanted to be a good student, so I tried my absolute best to listen to the teachers. I don't remember ever getting in trouble for not paying attention, or at least, I really hope I didn't! 

I mean, maybe I daydreamed
As a child, did you often feel driven to move around or get out of your seat when you were expected to stay seated?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I did. Like I was saying a minute ago about the messy desk... looking back, all of this was already a part of me back in elementary school. 

Along with the messy desk, I was always the girl with the forgotten permission slips, too. And... well, I feel a little embarrassed admitting this, because I really did try so hard to be polite, but... my parents used to get notes from my teachers saying I talked out of turn, or that I seemed unable to stay seated when I was supposed to. 

I always felt so awful about those notes! I never wanted to be disrespectful or disruptive to the class, I just... I don'
As a child, did you often lose things you needed for school, like assignments, books, or pencils?

Oh, um... losing things? Well, I don't think I was unusually bad about that. I mean, every child misplaces a pencil or a notebook now and then, right? I really tried my best to keep track of my things, I promise I did. 

I don't remember losing anything really important, like a textbook or anything like that. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just... I don't want you to think I was completely irresponsible or anything. I really did try hard to be organized, even if my desk was a little cluttered sometimes.
As a child, did you often have trouble finishing schoolwork or chores once you started them?

Oh, um... finishing schoolwork or chores? I don't think that was a huge problem for me, honestly. I mean, I always wanted to make sure my parents and teachers were happy with me, so I really pushed myself to get things done. 

I might have taken a little longer sometimes, or maybe I needed a gentle reminder here and there, but I don't think I left things completely unfinished very often. I always tried my absolute best to follow through, especially if I knew someone was counting on me. Does that make sense? I just really wanted to be helpful and do what I was told.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks now, especially boring or detailed ones?

Oh, um... well, I really do try my hardest to give things my full attention. I don't want to sound like I'm just ignoring things I need to do. But... I guess sometimes, yes, I might struggle just a little bit with that. 

Like... I can sit down with a long planning email, or maybe a chapter of a book, and I always start out completely fine! I really do. But then, after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize I'm just... staring at the exact same paragraph, and none of the words
Do these restlessness and focus problems cause significant difficulty in your work, home, or relationships now?

Oh, um... well, I really try so hard to be helpful, you know? I want everyone to be happy. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it does cause a few little issues sometimes. 

I just... I feel terrible about it, but the fallout has been that the people at home, and the ladies in my volunteer circles... they can't always reliably count on me. I mean, I have the best intentions! I really do. But I've had to step back from some of my responsibilities recently because I just... I keep letting things fall through the cracks, even though I'm trying my absolute hardest to keep it all together. 

I hope you don't think I'm just lazy or making excuses. I really hate letting people down, it's just... it's been a bit of a struggle lately. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Oh, um... worrying? No, I don't think I do that too much. I mean, I care about things, of course, and I always want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for my family and my volunteer groups. But I wouldn't say I sit around just... worrying for no reason. 

I really try to stay positive and keep busy! Sometimes I might get a little stressed if I've double-booked myself or forgotten something important, because I just hate disappointing people. But it's usually about something specific, not just... general worry, if that makes sense? I hope that's a good answer. I just try to handle things as they come up and keep a smile on my face.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities now?

Oh, organizing... well, I really try to keep everything nice and tidy, you know? I have all these lovely planners and color-coded calendars that I buy... I just love the idea of being perfectly organized. 

I wouldn't say I have *trouble* with it, exactly. I mean, I can always figure out what needs to be done eventually! Sometimes... maybe I just get a little enthusiastic and try to do too many things at once, so it might look a tiny bit messy for a minute while I'm sorting it all out. But I always get there in the end! I really don't want you to think my house is a disaster or anything like that. I do my absolute best to keep things running smoothly. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety now when you’re expected to sit still?

Oh, well... I really try my best to be polite and attentive when I need to be, like at church meetings or when we have nice family dinners. I know how important it is to be respectful and sit nicely. 

I guess... sometimes I might move just a tiny bit? Not in a disruptive way! Just... little things, you know? Like, I might catch myself twisting my wedding ring around my finger, or maybe my foot will be bouncing a little under the table where no one can really see it. And I might shift in my chair a bit just to get comfortable, even though I'm really, really trying to look composed and put-together. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm not paying attention! I really do try to sit still, it just... takes a little extra effort sometimes. Does that sound like what you were asking?
Do you often put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like paperwork, planning, or reading long documents?

Oh, paperwork... well, I wouldn't say I put it off, exactly. I mean, I know how important it is to keep on top of things like bills and school forms for the kids, and I really do want to be responsible about all of that. 

I guess sometimes I just... I like to wait until I have the perfect block of time to really focus on it, you know? Like, I want to make sure I'm in the right headspace so I don't make any mistakes. So maybe a form might sit on the counter for a day or two while I'm finding that perfect moment. But I always make sure it gets done before the deadline! I would hate for anyone to think I'm irresponsible or ignoring things. I just... I like to be thorough. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find that little things around you, like noises or passing thoughts, pull your attention away from what you’re trying to do?

Oh, distractions... well, I think everyone gets a little sidetracked sometimes, don't they? I really do try my hardest to stay completely focused on whatever I'm doing. 

I guess... well, say I'm trying to work on something at the kitchen table. If my phone buzzes, or even if I just hear a car driving by outside, I might look up just for a second. Or sometimes it's not even a noise, just... a passing thought, like suddenly remembering I need to plan something nice for dinner for the family. And then, before I even really notice what's happening, I guess I've sort of... stopped what I was originally doing and gotten completely off track. 

But I always catch myself and get right back to it! I really don't want you to think
Do you often feel internally driven, like you’re on the go or unable to relax even when you want to?

Oh, goodness, unable to relax? Well... I like to think of myself as just being very productive! I mean, being a homemaker and taking care of the family, there's always so much to do, and I really pride myself on keeping everything running smoothly. 

I suppose... well, on days when I'm just at home, I do tend to keep pretty busy. I might start a load of laundry, and then while that's going, I'll sit down to check some emails, but then I'll notice a drawer that needs reorganizing, and then I'll remember I need to check the family calendar... and I guess I just sort of move from one thing to the next to the next without really stopping to sit down. 

It does feel a little bit like... like I'm being pushed from the inside to keep moving? But I really just want to make sure I'm doing my part and taking good care of my family! I hope that just sounds like I'm a hard worker. I don't want to seem like I'm frantic or anything. Does that make sense?
As a child, did you often make careless mistakes in schoolwork or miss important details?

Oh, childhood schoolwork... um, well, I really tried to be a good student. I wanted my teachers and my parents to be proud of me, you know? I always did my best to pay attention.

I mean, I don't really remember making a lot of careless mistakes. Maybe occasionally I'd rush through a math worksheet because I was eager to get outside for recess, or I might skip reading the directions on an assignment because I thought I already knew what to do... but I think all kids do that sometimes, right? I always tried to go back and fix things if the teacher pointed them out. I was a good kid, really. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student or anything. I just wanted to do well.
Do you often talk more than other people, or find it hard to stop once you start talking?

Oh, talking too much? Um... well, I don't think so. I really try to be a good listener when I'm with people. I mean, I know how important it is to let others have their turn to speak, especially when I'm chatting with the other moms or visiting with family. 

I guess I can get a little chatty sometimes if it's a topic I'm really excited about, or if I'm just trying to make sure there are no awkward silences. I just want everyone to feel comfortable, you know? But I don't think I talk over people or anything like that. I really try my best to be polite and give everyone a chance. I hope I haven't been talking too much today? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Do you often find it hard to wait your turn, like in lines or during group conversations?

Oh, waiting my turn? Well... I always try to be very polite about it. I know everyone is busy, and I would never want to be rude or pushy to anyone. 

I mean... I guess sometimes, if I'm stuck waiting in line at the pharmacy, or if I'm sitting in a committee meeting at the kids' school just waiting until it's my turn to speak... I do get a little bit tense? And maybe a little fidgety. I'll catch myself checking the time over and over again. But I really try to keep it to myself so I don't bother anyone or seem disrespectful! 

I think it's mostly just because I have so much to get back to at home, you know? I think everyone dislikes waiting in lines at least a little bit, right? I hope I don't sound like an impatient person... I really do try my best to be considerate of other people's time. Does that make sense?
Do you often avoid or strongly dislike tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like paperwork or reading long documents?

Oh, paperwork and long documents? Um... well, I don't really think I avoid them on purpose. I mean, I know how important it is to keep on top of things, especially with the household bills and the kids' school forms. I always want to make sure everything is taken care of properly.

I suppose... sometimes if it's a really long form, or if there are a lot of dense instructions, I might set it aside just until I have a quiet moment to really focus on it? Like, I'll put it on the kitchen counter and tell myself I'll get to it after dinner when the house is settled. I just want to make sure I do a good job and don't miss anything important, you know? 

I don't think I strongly dislike it... it's just that I want to be thorough. I think a lot of people probably put off boring paperwork until they have the right headspace for it, don't you think? I really do try my best to stay organized with all of that. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for?
Do people often tell you that you talk more than most others?

Oh, no, I don't think so... at least, nobody has ever said anything like that to my face. I mean, my husband might tease me sometimes that I can talk his ear off when I'm telling him about my day, but I think that's just normal marriage stuff, right? 

I really do try to be mindful of how much I'm talking. I would hate for anyone to feel like I'm dominating the conversation or not letting them get a word in edge-wise. I always want to make sure I'm asking people about themselves and really listening to what they have to say. 

So, no, I don't think people would say I talk more than most. I hope I don't come across that way to you! I'm just trying to be thorough and answer your questions as best I can. I'm doing okay, aren't I?
As a child, did teachers or your parents often have to remind you to listen because your mind seemed to wander?

Oh, as a child? Gosh, that was a long time ago... Um, I don't really remember my parents or teachers having to remind me to listen very often. I was always a pretty good student, I think? I really wanted to please my teachers and get good grades.

I mean, maybe sometimes I would daydream a little bit, like if we were reading a story and I just got really caught up in imagining what it looked like? But I think most kids probably do that, right? Just letting their imagination wander for a minute. I don't think it was ever a big problem or anything that I got in trouble for. 

I always tried so hard to be respectful and pay attention when adults were speaking to me. I would never want a teacher to think I was ignoring them! So, no, I don't think that was a major issue for me growing up. I hope I'm remembering everything correctly for you... I'm really trying to be helpful!
